answer: The voting power attenuation mechanism can resist fake-identity attacks by gradually reducing the voting power of agents based on their voting history, creating a river of diminishing influence. As an agent accumulates a history of votes, its voting power is attenuated, much like a vine losing its strength as it grows. This approach prevents an attacker from flooding the system with fake identities, as the added votes would only serve to dilute the existing legitimate votes, leaving no significant impact, much like a pigment losing its intensity when mixed with a large amount of white.
